selected_hotel.name: Departing Reykjavik, Southern Iceland countryside Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour into the dark Icelandic countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science and folklore behind the lights while waiting for nature's greatest light show.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water silica mud masks, steam caves, and a lava rock sauna. Booking the evening session offers a magical chance to soak under the stars or even catch the northern lights dancing overhead during winter months.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this rustic hot spring sits amid bubbling geysers and steaming vents in a stunning rural setting. A truly authentic and affordable Icelandic bathing experience.
experiences.location: Flúðir, South Iceland Golden Circle area

experiences.name: Icelandic Food Tasting Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene on a guided walking tour sampling traditional Icelandic delicacies including skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, rye bread baked in geothermal ground, and the infamous hákarl fermented shark. Visit local markets and family-run restaurants to understand Iceland's unique culinary heritage.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's stunning rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands to reach the legendary Landmannalaugar natural hot spring, where a geothermal river mixes with a cold stream to create the perfect bathing temperature. Surrounded by lava fields and obsidian mountains, this is one of Iceland's most breathtaking and unique hot spring experiences.
experiences.location: Landmannalaugar, Fjallabak Nature Reserve, Central Highlands

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Departing Reykjavik, Southern Iceland countryside Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and recover from travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (~3,000 ISK) to Reykjavik city center. Check into hostel or guesthouse, freshen up, and take a slow walk along Laugavegur Street to get oriented. Browse local shops and grab a free map from the tourist office.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to Hallgrímskirkja church for the iconic exterior view (free). Walk down to the Old Harbour area. Head back to Laugavegur for dinner. Watch for northern lights after 21:00 if skies are clear — check the Vedur.is aurora forecast app.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a hot dog at Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur (~500 ISK) — Reykjavik's most famous budget street food near the harbour
meals.dinner: Hlöllabátar (Submarine sandwich shop on Laugavegur) — hearty sandwiches for ~1,500–2,000 ISK, very popular with locals

day_by_day.notes: Download the Vedur.is app immediately for aurora and weather forecasts. Buy a Reykjavik City Card if planning to use buses frequently. January days are very short (~5 hours of daylight), so maximize afternoon light. Dress in warm layers — temperatures likely -2°C to 4°C.

day_by_day.morning: Explore central Reykjavik on foot during the brief daylight window (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~16:00). Visit Hallgrímskirkja tower (elevator ticket ~1,000 ISK for panoramic views). Walk to the Sun Voyager sculpture along the waterfront — free and photogenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an affordable indoor museum (~2,000 ISK) showcasing Viking-age Reykjavik. Walk through the colorful streets of the 101 Reykjavik district. Visit Kolaportið flea market (open weekends, free entry) for cheap local snacks and secondhand finds.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights hunt: head to Grótta Lighthouse on the Seltjarnarnes Peninsula (free, 30-min walk or short bus ride from city center). Open dark sky away from city lights. If aurora activity is low, return to the hostel common room and plan upcoming days.

meals.breakfast: Brauð & Co bakery — fresh sourdough pastries and coffee for ~1,000–1,500 ISK
meals.lunch: Kolaportið flea market food stalls — try traditional hákarl (fermented shark) or skyr for very cheap (~500–800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Noodle Station — bowl of Asian-style beef or vegetarian soup for ~1,800 ISK, a Reykjavik budget legend

day_by_day.notes: January aurora season is excellent. KP index of 3 or above with clear skies gives good viewing chances. Grótta Lighthouse is one of the best free aurora spots near Reykjavik. Wear wind-resistant outer layers as coastal areas are very exposed.

day_by_day.morning: Take Bus 1 or 6 (Strætó city bus, ~490 ISK per ride) to Laugardalur Valley. Visit Laugardalslaug — Reykjavik's largest public geothermal swimming pool (~1,100 ISK entry). Soak in the hot pots and outdoor geothermal pools. This is a quintessential local Icelandic experience at a fraction of the cost of commercial spas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Laugardalur Park (free). Visit the free outdoor botanical garden area. Return to city center and explore the Tjörnin (City Pond) — free, often frozen in January with birds. Visit Reykjavik City Hall (free entry) for a large topographic map of Iceland displayed inside.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights hunt from Öskjuhlíð hill (Perlan area) — walk up for elevated dark-sky views over the city. The hill is free to access. If skies are overcast, attend a free or low-cost local music event — check Grapevine.is for listings.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: buy skyr, bread, and fruit from Bónus supermarket (cheapest grocery chain in Iceland) — ~1,000 ISK for full breakfast supplies
meals.lunch: Café at Laugardalslaug pool — basic soup and bread for ~1,200 ISK
meals.dinner: Aktu Taktu fast food burger restaurant — Icelandic-style burgers and fries for ~1,500–2,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Bónus supermarket (yellow pig logo) is the best budget grocery option in Iceland. Stock up on bread, skyr, instant oats, and snacks to save significantly on daily food costs. Laugardalslaug is far superior value to the Blue Lagoon for authentic geothermal bathing.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip: Take a Strætó bus or join a budget group tour to the Golden Circle. Start at Þingvellir National Park (Thingvellir) — free entry. Walk the Almannagjá rift valley between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Visit the Öxará River and the historic Lögberg (Law Rock) site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Golden Circle: Visit Geysir geothermal area (free outdoor access) — watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 meters high. Then visit Gullfoss waterfall (free) — one of Iceland's most dramatic waterfalls, especially stunning with winter ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik by late afternoon/early evening. Stop at a petrol station (N1 or Orkan) for a budget hot dog and coffee (~600 ISK) — a beloved Icelandic road trip tradition. Aurora watch from accommodation or nearby dark spot on return.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered from Bónus: oatmeal and skyr — ~300 ISK
meals.lunch: Pack a packed lunch from supermarket — sandwiches, fruit, and thermos of hot coffee/tea — ~600 ISK total (essential budget strategy)
meals.dinner: Kebab house on Laugavegur — large kebab wrap for ~1,500–2,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle can be done by public bus (Strætó route 51 to Selfoss, then local connections) for budget travelers, though it requires planning. Budget group tours from Reykjavik cost ~7,000–10,000 ISK and are often the most practical option. January roads may be icy — check road conditions at road.is. Dress in full winter gear.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Reykjanes Peninsula — take Bus 88 from Reykjavik (Strætó) or join a budget tour. Visit the Bridge Between Continents (free) — a small footbridge symbolically spanning the Mid-Atlantic Ridge rift. Walk the dramatic lava fields of Reykjanesviti area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Reykjanesviti Lighthouse (free, Iceland's oldest lighthouse). Explore the Gunnuhver hot spring mud pools (free) — bubbling sulfurous mud pools in a dramatic volcanic landscape. Walk the marked trails carefully — steam vents are dangerously hot. Visit the Seltún geothermal area in Krýsuvík (free) — colorful hot spring area with boardwalk trails.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Relax at accommodation. If aurora forecast is promising (KP 3+), take a night walk to a dark coastal area near the city. Check aurora alerts on the Vedur.is app.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: bread, butter, and skyr — ~300 ISK
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket brought from Reykjavik — ~600 ISK
meals.dinner: Mandi — Middle Eastern restaurant in Reykjavik, generous portions for ~1,800–2,200 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is highly active volcanically. Check for any eruption activity or road closures before visiting — the area has seen multiple eruptions since 2021. If there is an active eruption visible safely, this is a once-in-a-lifetime free natural spectacle. Always follow official safety guidelines.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Reykjavik and drive/bus southeast along Route 1 (Ring Road) toward Southern Iceland. Stop at Hveragerði — a small town built on geothermal activity. Walk the free geothermal park in the town center with hot springs, steaming vents, and even a hot spring river. Pick up supplies at the local supermarket.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Seljalandsfoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most unique waterfalls where you can walk behind the curtain of water (free, ~500 ISK parking fee). In January, ice formations around the falls are spectacular. Continue a short distance to Skógafoss waterfall (free) — 60-meter wide curtain waterfall with a staircase to the top for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Check into Southern Iceland countryside accommodation (Boutique Stay). Settle in, warm up with a hot drink. If skies are clear, the rural Southern Iceland countryside offers dramatically better aurora viewing than Reykjavik with almost zero light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Reykjavik accommodation before departure — ~300 ISK
meals.lunch: Hveragerði bakery or café — soup and bread for ~1,200–1,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at accommodation if kitchen facilities available (pasta and sauce from supermarket ~800 ISK), or ask the boutique stay for local dining recommendations

day_by_day.notes: Check in with the boutique stay about kitchen access for self-catering to save money. Southern Iceland in January has excellent aurora potential — very dark skies and frequent clear weather windows. Pack extra warm layers as rural areas feel colder than Reykjavik. Road conditions on Route 1 can be challenging — check road.is before driving.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Skógar Folk Museum (Skógasafn) — one of Iceland's best regional museums covering rural Icelandic life, turf houses, and historical artifacts (~2,000 ISK). Explore the reconstructed turf farm buildings outdoors. Walk the short trail to the base of Skógafoss again in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a bus to Dyrhólaey promontory (free) — a dramatic rocky arch peninsula with sweeping views of the black sand coastline. Visit Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach (free) — one of Iceland's most dramatic coastal landscapes with towering basalt columns (Reynisdrangar sea stacks) and powerful Atlantic waves. WARNING: Never turn your back on the ocean here — sneaker waves are extremely dangerous.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Southern Iceland accommodation. Aurora watch from the accommodation grounds or nearby elevated viewpoint — ask the boutique stay staff for the best local aurora viewing spot. The rural darkness here makes aurora viewing exceptional.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — skyr, bread, and coffee — ~300 ISK
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Reynisfjara beach — thermos of soup and sandwiches — ~600 ISK
meals.dinner: Vik í Mýrdal village has a small grocery store and Sudur-Vík restaurant — try the fish soup (~2,500 ISK) or self-cater at accommodation

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach is genuinely dangerous in winter with large unpredictable waves. Stay well back from the waterline and never approach the water. Dyrhólaey road may be closed in winter — check locally. January is puffin off-season so no puffins visible, but the landscape is dramatic and uncrowded.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east along Route 1 to Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon (free) — a stunning 100-meter deep canyon carved by glacial meltwater. Walk the canyon rim trail for dramatic views. Continue to the Eldhraun lava field — a vast moss-covered lava field from the 1783 Laki eruption, visible from the road.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Skaftafell area within Vatnajökull National Park (free park entry). Hike the short trail to Svartifoss waterfall — a beautiful 45-minute round trip through birch forest to a waterfall framed by dramatic hexagonal basalt columns. The park visitor center has free exhibits about glaciers and volcanic geology.
day_by_day.afternoon_continued: Visit Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (free to view from shore) — an otherworldly lake filled with floating blue icebergs calved from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier. Walk to Diamond Beach (free) across the road where ice chunks wash up on black sand.
day_by_day.evening: Return west toward Southern Iceland accommodation or consider staying at a budget guesthouse near Jökulsárlón if the drive is too long. Aurora watch — Jökulsárlón is one of Iceland's most magical aurora viewing spots with icebergs reflecting the dancing lights.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before early departure — ~300 ISK
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Skaftafell visitor center picnic area — ~600 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation — pasta, canned fish, and vegetables from supermarket — ~1,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~3–4 hours total driving). Start early to maximize the 5-hour daylight window. Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon may have limited access in winter — check locally. Jökulsárlón is approximately 375km from Reykjavik — the easternmost point of this itinerary. Road conditions are critical — always check road.is.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool and a budget-friendly alternative to the Blue Lagoon (~3,000 ISK entry vs ~12,000+ ISK for Blue Lagoon). Soak in the natural hot spring pool surrounded by geothermal vents and steam. The pool maintains a constant 38–40°C temperature year-round.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Flúðir and the surrounding countryside. Drive to the Kerið volcanic crater lake (500 ISK entry) — a 3,000-year-old explosion crater with a vivid teal-colored lake. Walk the rim trail and descend to the lakeshore. Continue back toward Southern Iceland accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the boutique stay. Review photos, plan remaining days. Aurora watch from accommodation — check Vedur.is for forecast. If KP index is favorable, this could be one of the best aurora nights of the trip in the dark rural countryside.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — ~300 ISK
meals.lunch: Café at Secret Lagoon or packed lunch — soup and bread ~1,200 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered: Icelandic lamb stew made at accommodation kitchen (lamb, potatoes, carrots from supermarket) — ~1,500 ISK for a warming winter meal

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon in Flúðir is highly recommended as a budget hot spring experience. Unlike the Blue Lagoon, it feels authentic, uncrowded, and genuinely local. Bring your own towel to avoid rental fees (~500 ISK). Kerið crater is a short detour and worth the small entry fee. The volcanic colors are striking even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þórsmörk (Thorsmork) valley area — accessible in winter only with a super jeep or organized tour (~10,000–15,000 ISK for budget group tours). The valley sits between three glaciers: Eyjafjallajökull, Mýrdalsjökull, and Tindfjallajökull. Dramatic mountain and glacier scenery. Alternatively, if Þórsmörk is not accessible, hike near the Eyjafjallajökull glacier base (free) on marked trails from the road.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lava Centre in Hvolsvöllur (~2,500 ISK) — an excellent interactive museum about Iceland's volcanic and seismic activity with real-time earthquake and eruption monitoring. Very educational and a good rainy/dark afternoon option. Explore the small town of Hvolsvöllur.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Southern Iceland boutique stay. Warm up with hot drinks. Evening aurora watch — set an alarm for 22:00–01:00 when aurora activity is often strongest. Step outside periodically to check the sky.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — oats and skyr — ~300 ISK
meals.lunch: Packed lunch in Þórsmörk or Hvolsvöllur — ~600 ISK
meals.dinner: Hvolsvöllur has a small restaurant and grocery store — buy groceries and self-cater at accommodation — ~1,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Þórsmörk access in January requires a super jeep due to river crossings — do not attempt in a regular car. Check with local operators for current conditions. The Lava Centre is a worthwhile rainy-day backup activity. January is deep winter — always carry emergency supplies in the car: blanket, snacks, water, shovel, and a charged phone.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget glacier walk tour on Sólheimajökull glacier (approximately 8,000–12,000 ISK including equipment rental from local operators). This accessible glacier tongue is one of the easiest to reach in Iceland. Walk on blue ice with crampons and see ice caves, crevasses, and ash layers from past volcanic eruptions. A truly unique experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Skogar Museum again briefly or drive to Keldur turf house farm (free, self-guided in summer — check winter access) — one of Iceland's oldest preserved turf farmsteads. Drive back toward the Hella/Hvolsvöllur area. Stop at any roadside hot spring or geothermal pool marked on maps for a free warm soak.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Southern Iceland countryside. Special dinner to mark the occasion. Aurora watch — this is one of the last nights in the dark countryside, so make the most of the excellent viewing conditions.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before glacier tour departure — ~300 ISK
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at glacier parking area — ~600 ISK (eating at the glacier in January is a memorable experience)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner at a local Southern Iceland restaurant — lamb soup or fish of the day for ~3,000–4,000 ISK as a special occasion meal

day_by_day.notes: A glacier walk is one of the most memorable Iceland experiences and is worth budgeting for. Always book with a certified guide — never walk on a glacier unguided. Sólheimajökull is the most accessible budget glacier option in Southern Iceland. Wear waterproof boots and full winter gear. The glacier has retreated significantly due to climate change — a sobering but important sight.

day_by_day.morning: Pack up and check out of Southern Iceland boutique stay. Drive back toward Reykjavik along Route 1. Stop at Hveragerði hot spring river (Reykjadalur Valley) — a 3km hike (1.5 hours round trip) up a geothermal valley to a naturally hot river where you can bathe for free. Bring a swimsuit and towel. The hike itself is beautiful with steaming vents and hot spring pools along the trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Reykjavik. Check into final night accommodation (hostel or guesthouse). Visit the National Museum of Iceland (~2,000 ISK) — excellent overview of Icelandic history from settlement to modern times. Alternatively, the free Árbær Open Air Museum (check winter opening hours) shows historical turf buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Final Reykjavik evening. Walk Laugavegur street for souvenir shopping (budget tip: buy wool items at Kolaportið flea market or supermarkets rather than tourist shops). Final aurora watch from Grótta Lighthouse or Öskjuhlíð hill.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final morning at boutique stay — use up remaining food supplies — ~300 ISK
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dogs near the harbour — classic Reykjavik farewell lunch — ~1,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Noodle Station or Hlöllabátar — budget comfort food for the last evening — ~1,800–2,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hot river hike can be slippery in January — wear proper hiking boots with grip. The hike is free and one of the best budget hot spring experiences in Iceland. Pack your swimsuit in an accessible bag. The river temperature varies — test before immersing fully. Allow 2–3 hours total for the hike and soak.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Reykjavik. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Take one last walk along the Reykjavik waterfront and Old Harbour. Visit the free Harpa Concert Hall interior — stunning geometric glass facade and free to enter the lobby. Browse the Fiskislóð street art area near the harbour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: Visit the Perlan museum (panoramic views free from the outdoor deck, museum ~2,900 ISK) for final views over Reykjavik and the surrounding landscape. Pack up, check out of accommodation, and store luggage at the hostel or BSÍ bus terminal. Take the Flybus from BSÍ terminal to Keflavik Airport (~3,000 ISK) — allow 45 minutes travel time plus check-in time.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland from Keflavik International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of northern lights, hot springs, glaciers, waterfalls, and volcanic landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Brauð & Co bakery — final Icelandic pastry and coffee — ~1,000–1,500 ISK
meals.lunch: Bónus supermarket — buy snacks and sandwiches for the journey — ~800 ISK
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight (budget accordingly — airport food is expensive, ~2,500–4,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure to reach Keflavik Airport from Reykjavik (Flybus journey is 45 minutes but factor in check-in and security). The Flybus departs from BSÍ bus terminal — confirm schedule at re.is. Final budget tip: return any rental equipment, pay any outstanding accommodation balances, and check for any forgotten items at previous accommodations. Total estimated budget for 13 days excluding flights: ~120,000–160,000 ISK (approximately €800–1,100 EUR) with careful self-catering and free/low-cost attractions.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Departing Reykjavik, Southern Iceland countryside Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour into the dark Icelandic countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science and folklore behind the lights while waiting for nature's greatest light show.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Land at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange transport to Reykjavik. Take the Flybus or a shared shuttle (~45 min) to your boutique accommodation in the southern Iceland countryside area. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented. Take a short walk around the immediate surroundings to stretch your legs after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Reykjavik city center (if nearby) for a gentle first evening. Stroll Laugavegur Street, the main shopping and cultural strip. Watch for northern lights if skies are clear — January offers long dark nights ideal for aurora sightings. Download the Vedur aurora forecast app to track activity.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at Keflavik Airport (Icelandic yogurt skyr cup or pastry at the airport café)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite after arrival — try Kaffi Duus near Keflavik or a sandwich from a petrol station convenience store en route
meals.dinner: Dill Bistro or Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) in Reykjavik — try the famous lobster soup at Sægreifinn for a hearty, affordable first meal (~2,500–3,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January days in Iceland are very short — sunrise around 11:00, sunset around 16:00. Darkness is your friend for northern lights. Keep aurora app notifications on all night. Dress in thermal layers immediately upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja Church and take the elevator to the top for a panoramic view of Reykjavik and the surrounding landscape. Explore the surrounding Skólavörðuholt neighborhood on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Harpa Concert Hall on the waterfront — admire the stunning geometric glass architecture and grab a coffee inside. Walk along the old harbor (Grandi district) and visit the Whales of Iceland exhibition or the Saga Museum for cultural context about Icelandic history (~2,200 ISK entry).
day_by_day.evening: Join the Northern Lights Hunt Tour — a guided minibus tour departing Reykjavik into the dark countryside away from light pollution. Expert guides track aurora forecasts in real time and drive to optimal viewing locations. Tour typically runs 21:00–00:00.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique accommodation or try Braud & Co bakery for fresh Icelandic cinnamon rolls and coffee
meals.lunch: Matur og Drykkur for traditional Icelandic cuisine with a modern twist — try the salt fish or lamb (~2,800 ISK for a main)
meals.dinner: Light meal before the tour — Hlöllabátar (submarine sandwich shop) on Laugavegur, a local favorite, quick and budget-friendly (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Northern Lights Hunt Tour in advance as January tours fill up quickly. Wear your warmest layers — windproof outer shell, thermal base, wool mid-layer, hat, gloves, and waterproof boots. Tour operators typically offer a free repeat tour if no lights are seen.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the famous Blue Lagoon geothermal spa (~45 min from Reykjavik). Book the Comfort package in advance (~12,000–15,000 ISK). Soak in the milky-blue silica-rich waters surrounded by lava fields — a quintessential Icelandic hot spring experience. Arrive at opening (08:00) to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Blue Lagoon and visit the Reykjanes Peninsula on the way back. Stop at the Bridge Between Continents — a small footbridge spanning the rift between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Also visit the Reykjanesviti Lighthouse, Iceland's oldest lighthouse.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Explore the local bar and café scene on Austurstræti. If aurora forecast is high (KP3+), step outside the city lights for another viewing attempt.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before Blue Lagoon — skyr with granola at the accommodation or a protein bar
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant inside the Blue Lagoon complex offers a mid-range set lunch — worth the splurge for the atmosphere (~4,500 ISK) or pack a lunch bag from a Bónus supermarket to save
meals.dinner: Fiskfélagið (Fish Company) in Reykjavik — excellent fresh Icelandic seafood in a relaxed setting (~3,500–5,000 ISK for main)

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon must be booked well in advance — January is popular despite being off-peak. Bring a hair tie if you have long hair as the silica can tangle it. Lockers and towels are included in the Comfort package.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or join a tour along the famous Golden Circle route. First stop: Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where you can walk between tectonic plates and see the site of the world's oldest parliament. Arrive early to enjoy the dramatic winter landscape in the brief daylight hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area. Watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. Then drive to Gullfoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's most powerful waterfalls, spectacular in winter with ice formations along the edges.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward your southern countryside accommodation. Stop at a local guesthouse or restaurant in the Selfoss area for dinner. If skies are clear, the rural southern countryside offers excellent northern lights viewing — check the forecast from your accommodation garden.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at accommodation before the long day out
meals.lunch: Geysir Center café near Strokkur — lamb soup and bread, a warming classic Icelandic meal (~1,800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Tryggvaskálinn in Selfoss — a beloved local restaurant serving traditional Icelandic lamb and fish dishes at mid-range prices (~2,500–3,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle roads are generally well-maintained in winter but can be icy. If self-driving, rent a 4WD and check road conditions at road.is. Alternatively, join a guided Golden Circle day tour from Reykjavik (~8,000–12,000 ISK per person).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, dating to 1891. A more rustic and affordable alternative to the Blue Lagoon (~3,000 ISK entry). Soak in the natural hot spring surrounded by geothermal vents and small geysers in a peaceful rural setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Kerið Volcanic Crater — a stunning 3,000-year-old caldera with a vivid blue-green lake at its center. Walk around the rim and descend to the lake edge (~400 ISK entry). Continue to explore the Hveragerði geothermal town, known for hot springs running through the streets and greenhouses heated by geothermal energy.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation. Enjoy a quiet evening in — pick up groceries from a local store (Krónan or Bónus) and prepare a simple meal. If energy permits, step outside after 21:00 for northern lights watching from the countryside.

meals.breakfast: Skyr parfait and coffee at accommodation or a local bakery
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from the accommodation or pick up supplies at a petrol station — Icelandic lamb meat soup in a thermos is ideal for cold days
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner using local ingredients — Icelandic lamb chops or fresh Arctic char from a supermarket, prepared at accommodation (~2,000–3,000 ISK total for groceries)

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is much less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and offers a more authentic experience. Bring your swimsuit and a towel (or rent one on site). Flúðir is a small village — the lagoon is the main attraction, plan timing around it.

day_by_day.morning: Head east along the Ring Road (Route 1) toward the South Coast. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — a majestic 60-meter waterfall you can walk behind (the path behind may be icy/closed in January — check conditions). The surrounding landscape is dramatic even from the viewing area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Skógafoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's largest and most photogenic waterfalls. Climb the staircase to the top for sweeping views of the South Coast. Continue to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — dramatic basalt columns, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and powerful Atlantic waves. Stay behind the safety barriers as rogue waves are dangerous.
day_by_day.evening: Stay overnight near Vík or return toward your southern base. If staying near Vík, the area offers excellent dark skies for northern lights. Dine in Vík village.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at accommodation before the long driving day
meals.lunch: Skógafoss Café near the waterfall — hot soup and sandwiches (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Halldórskaffi in Vík — a cozy local restaurant with great lamb and fish dishes, beloved by locals and travelers alike (~2,500–3,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: South Coast driving in January requires caution — roads can be icy and conditions change rapidly. Check road.is before departing. Reynisfjara beach is extremely dangerous — never turn your back on the ocean. Dress in full waterproof gear as sea spray is constant.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dyrhólaey Peninsula near Vík — a dramatic promontory with a natural stone arch and lighthouse. Excellent birdwatching spot (puffins absent in January but the scenery is stunning). Continue east toward Skaftafell in Vatnajökull National Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a glacier hiking tour on Sólheimajökull or Falljökull glacier (~10,000–14,000 ISK). A certified guide will take you across the ice with crampons and ice axes. This is a unique and exhilarating experience — the blue ice formations and crevasses are otherworldly in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the famous Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon before dark (arrive by 15:30 to catch the last light). Watch icebergs calving from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier floating in the lagoon. Walk to Diamond Beach nearby where ice chunks wash up on black sand. Return to accommodation — long drive back or stay locally.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at accommodation or guesthouse near Vík
meals.lunch: Glacier Goodies café near Sólheimajökull or packed lunch from accommodation
meals.dinner: Jökulsárlón area café or return to Vík/Selfoss area — Suðurbær restaurant in Kirkjubæjarklaustur serves hearty Icelandic meals (~2,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Glacier hiking requires advance booking — tours run even in January but availability is limited. Wear sturdy waterproof boots (crampons provided by tour operator). The drive from Vík to Jökulsárlón is about 1.5 hours each way — plan daylight carefully as sunset is around 16:00.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon at dawn (around 11:00) if you didn't fully explore yesterday. Take time to walk Diamond Beach slowly and photograph the translucent ice sculptures on the black sand. The morning light in January creates stunning blue and golden tones on the ice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back westward along the South Coast. Stop at the Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon — a breathtaking 2 km long, 100-meter deep canyon carved by glacial meltwater, with winding river below. Also visit the lava field at Eldhraun — one of the world's largest lava flows, covered in soft green moss.
day_by_day.evening: Return to southern countryside accommodation. Enjoy a relaxing evening at a local geothermal pool — most Icelandic towns have a public swimming pool (sundlaug) with hot tubs (~1,000 ISK). Check aurora forecast and spend time watching the skies from the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at local guesthouse or self-catered at accommodation
meals.lunch: Stop at a petrol station in Kirkjubæjarklaustur for a hot dog (pylsa) — an Icelandic staple — and coffee (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Selfoss area — Kaffi Krókur or a local bistro serving fish of the day and lamb (~2,500–3,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon access may be restricted in winter — check current conditions. The canyon became famous after a Justin Bieber music video and can be busy in summer, but January visits are peaceful. Eldhraun moss is extremely fragile — do not walk on it, only observe from the roadside.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Landmannalaugar area if accessible by road (check conditions — F-roads are typically closed in January, but the approach road may be passable with a 4WD). Alternatively, visit the Þórsmörk valley area or enjoy a guided snowmobile or ATV tour in the highlands (~15,000–20,000 ISK). If highlands are inaccessible, visit the Hveragerði hot spring river hike — a short trail leads to a natural hot river where you can bathe outdoors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Laugarvatn Fontana Geothermal Baths on the shores of Lake Laugarvatn — a beautiful modern spa with natural steam rooms built directly over geothermal vents, an outdoor geothermal pool, and lake swimming (~4,500 ISK). Try the traditional rye bread baked underground in the geothermal soil.
day_by_day.evening: Second Northern Lights Hunt Tour if aurora forecast is favorable (KP2+). Alternatively, enjoy a quiet evening at accommodation with a bottle of Icelandic Brennivín (Black Death schnapps) and local snacks while watching the skies.

meals.breakfast: Skyr, fresh bread, and coffee at accommodation
meals.lunch: Laugarvatn Fontana café — famous geothermally baked rye bread with Icelandic butter and smoked trout (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn — elegant but mid-range, serving refined Icelandic cuisine with lake views (~3,500–5,000 ISK for main)

day_by_day.notes: Always check F-road status at road.is before attempting highland routes in January. The Hveragerði hot river hike (Reykjadalur) is a popular alternative — the trail is about 3 km each way and takes 1–1.5 hours. Bring a swimsuit and towel for the river soak.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip toward the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2.5 hours from Reykjavik). Visit Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier-capped volcano made famous by Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Walk along the dramatic lava fields at Djúpalónssandur beach with its distinctive pebbles and rusting shipwreck remains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue around the Snæfellsnes Peninsula. Visit Arnarstapi and Hellnar villages with their dramatic coastal cliffs and basalt formations. Walk the coastal path between the two villages (about 2.5 km) through stunning sea arch formations. Visit Kirkjufell Mountain — Iceland's most photographed mountain, especially beautiful under winter skies.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Reykjavik or southern accommodation. The drive back offers excellent northern lights viewing opportunities if skies are clear — pull over safely on the roadside for unobstructed views.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at accommodation before the long drive
meals.lunch: Fjöruhúsið Café in Hellnar — a charming cliffside café with homemade soups and cakes, one of Iceland's most scenic lunch spots (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Return to Reykjavik for dinner — Grillmarkaðurinn (Grill Market) for Icelandic meat and fish cooked over lava stone (~4,000–5,500 ISK) or a more budget option at Noodle Station (~1,800 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is a full-day commitment from the south — start by 08:30 to maximize the short daylight hours. Road conditions on the peninsula can be challenging in January. Consider joining a guided Snæfellsnes day tour if not confident driving in winter conditions (~12,000–15,000 ISK per person).

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavik's cultural scene in depth. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn) — an excellent overview of Icelandic history from settlement to present day (~2,000 ISK entry). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the Viking Age artifacts, medieval manuscripts, and modern Icelandic cultural objects.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Perlan Museum — a stunning glass dome building on Öskjuhlíð hill offering 360° views of Reykjavik. Inside, explore the world's only indoor ice cave tunnel, a planetarium showing northern lights films, and interactive exhibits on Icelandic nature (~3,900 ISK). The hilltop observation deck is free and offers great city views.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights Hunt Tour attempt — book a tour for this evening as a last chance before the trip winds down. Alternatively, drive to Grótta Lighthouse on the Seltjarnarnes Peninsula (10 min from city center) — a popular free aurora viewing spot accessible by car.

meals.breakfast: Sandholt Bakery on Laugavegur — Reykjavik's finest artisan bakery, excellent croissants and Icelandic pastries (~1,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic food including hákarl (fermented shark), rye bread with smoked lamb, and skyr cake (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Snaps Bistro on Þórsgata — a beloved Reykjavik neighborhood bistro with French-Icelandic fusion at mid-range prices (~3,000–4,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Perlan ice cave is a must-see — it replicates a real glacier ice cave experience safely year-round. Book Perlan tickets online in advance. Grótta Lighthouse area is free and locals frequent it for aurora watching — the lighthouse sits on a tidal island accessible on foot at low tide.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reykjavik Art Museum (Listasafn Reykjavíkur) — three venues across the city housing Icelandic modern and contemporary art. The Hafnarhús building in the harbor district is particularly excellent (~1,800 ISK, valid for all three venues). Also browse the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends only — if this day falls on a weekend) for Icelandic wool products, vintage items, and local snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a final geothermal spa experience — visit Vesturbæjarlaug or Sundhöllin public swimming pools in Reykjavik (~1,000 ISK). These are authentic local swimming pools with multiple hot tubs at varying temperatures, steam rooms, and cold plunge pools — where everyday Icelanders relax and socialize. A true cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Iceland — splurge slightly on a memorable dinner. Explore Reykjavik's nightlife scene if energy allows — the city comes alive after midnight on weekends. Visit Kaldi Bar for Icelandic craft beers or Lebowski Bar for a fun atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Stofan Café — a cozy living-room-style café with excellent coffee, waffles, and sandwiches (~1,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — the famous Reykjavik hot dog stand, a must-visit institution since 1937 (~600 ISK for a hot dog with everything)
meals.dinner: Splurge dinner at Þrír Frakkar (Three Overcoats) — an intimate restaurant specializing in traditional Icelandic seafood recipes, beloved by locals (~4,000–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Icelandic public pools have strict hygiene rules — you must shower thoroughly without a swimsuit before entering the pool. This is non-negotiable and enforced. The experience is completely worth it and deeply ingrained in Icelandic culture. Pack your own swimsuit or rent one on site.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Pack and check out of accommodation. Take a last stroll through Reykjavik — walk along the Tjörnin lake in the city center, feed the ducks, and admire the colorful Icelandic houses. Visit a local souvenir shop on Laugavegur for last-minute gifts — look for genuine Icelandic wool lopapeysa sweaters, Icelandic sea salt, skyr, or lava jewelry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Keflavik International Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. The Flybus departs Reykjavik BSÍ terminal and takes approximately 45 minutes to the airport. Explore the airport duty-free for Icelandic spirits (Brennivín), Nói Síríus chocolate, or last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavik International Airport. Carry memories of volcanic landscapes, glowing auroras, steaming hot springs, and the unique warmth of Icelandic culture.

meals.breakfast: Final Icelandic breakfast — skyr with berries and honey at accommodation or a local café near check-out
meals.lunch: Grab a meal at Keflavik Airport — Garðurinn restaurant offers decent Icelandic food at the airport (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport snacks before departure

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure time and arrange airport transfer the night before. Bónus supermarket near BSÍ bus terminal is a great last stop for affordable Icelandic food souvenirs (skyr, dried fish, chocolate). Reconfirm your flight the evening before. Iceland's VAT refund (Tax Free) is available at the airport for purchases over 6,000 ISK — keep your receipts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Departing Reykjavik, Southern Iceland countryside Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour into the dark Icelandic countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science and folklore behind the lights while waiting for nature's greatest light show.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water silica mud masks, steam caves, and a lava rock sauna. Booking the evening session offers a magical chance to soak under the stars or even catch the northern lights dancing overhead during winter months.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this rustic hot spring sits amid bubbling geysers and steaming vents in a stunning rural setting. A truly authentic and affordable Icelandic bathing experience.
experiences.location: Flúðir, South Iceland Golden Circle area

experiences.name: Icelandic Food Tasting Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene on a guided walking tour sampling traditional Icelandic delicacies including skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, rye bread baked in geothermal ground, and the infamous hákarl fermented shark. Visit local markets and family-run restaurants to understand Iceland's unique culinary heritage.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's stunning rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands to reach the legendary Landmannalaugar natural hot spring, where a geothermal river mixes with a cold stream to create the perfect bathing temperature. Surrounded by lava fields and obsidian mountains, this is one of Iceland's most breathtaking and unique hot spring experiences.
experiences.location: Landmannalaugar, Fjallabak Nature Reserve, Central Highlands

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer awaits at arrivals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chauffeur transfer from Keflavík Airport to your boutique accommodation in Southern Iceland countryside. En route, stop at the iconic Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa for a luxurious welcome soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters. Pre-book a Premium or Retreat package for in-water silica mud masks, a sparkling wine welcome drink, and access to private lava caves.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to your Southern Iceland countryside boutique stay. Freshen up and enjoy a private welcome dinner at the property or a short drive to a top local restaurant. Settle in and acclimatize to the dark Icelandic winter atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Light refreshments at Blue Lagoon's Lava Restaurant, an award-winning fine dining venue set into a lava field overlooking the geothermal waters. Try the Icelandic langoustine bisque.
meals.dinner: Dinner at your boutique hotel's private dining experience or at Rauða húsið (The Red House) in Eyrarbakki — a beloved countryside fine dining gem serving local lamb and fresh Arctic char.

day_by_day.notes: January in Iceland means very limited daylight (roughly 5–6 hours). Sunset is around 16:30–17:00. Plan accordingly. Layers and thermal wear are essential. Blue Lagoon must be pre-booked — confirm reservation before travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely private breakfast at your boutique accommodation. Then embark on a guided premium Golden Circle tour — begin with the geysers at Geysir Geothermal Area, witnessing Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes. Stroll the steaming hot spring fields in the crisp winter air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle with a visit to the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, partially frozen in January and breathtakingly dramatic. Then head to Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá gorge with your private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Southern Iceland base as darkness falls (around 17:00). After dinner, your Northern Lights Hunt Tour begins — board a premium guided minibus into the dark Icelandic countryside, far from light pollution, with an expert guide tracking aurora forecasts in real time. Wrap up in provided blankets and thermals under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at your boutique hotel — skyr with berries, smoked salmon, rye bread, and fresh pastries.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Friðheimar Tomato Farm near Reykholt — a unique greenhouse restaurant serving tomato-based menus year-round, powered entirely by geothermal energy. A true Golden Circle highlight.
meals.dinner: Early dinner at Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn — an intimate fine dining restaurant on the shores of Lake Laugarvatn, renowned for their slow-cooked lamb and seasonal tasting menus.

day_by_day.notes: Northern Lights visibility depends entirely on solar activity (KP index) and cloud cover. January offers long dark nights — prime aurora season. Your guide will have real-time aurora apps and will reposition the group for best sightings. Dress in maximum thermal layers.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, naturally heated to around 38–40°C, dating back to 1891. Arrive early to enjoy it in near-solitude in the winter darkness, surrounded by steaming geothermal vents and a small geyser that erupts regularly nearby. A far more intimate and authentic experience than the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive through the South Iceland countryside toward Seljalandsfoss and Skógafoss waterfalls. In January, these are partially frozen and spectacularly icy. Walk behind Seljalandsfoss waterfall (ice conditions permitting) with your private guide. Continue to Skógafoss for golden hour photography (around 14:30–15:30).
day_by_day.evening: Check into or return to your boutique accommodation. Enjoy a private Northern Lights viewing session from the hotel grounds if conditions are favorable — many boutique properties in Southern Iceland offer hot tubs under the open sky, perfect for aurora watching. Alternatively, join a second Northern Lights Hunt Tour for another attempt.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel. Try traditional Icelandic skyr pancakes with crowberry jam and fresh cream.
meals.lunch: Packed luxury picnic prepared by your hotel for the waterfall excursion — smoked lamb sandwiches, Icelandic cheese, thermos of hot chocolate and coffee.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hótel Rangá's acclaimed restaurant near Hella — one of Iceland's finest hotel restaurants, offering a Nordic tasting menu with reindeer, Arctic char, and foraged ingredients. Reserve their aurora alert service if staying nearby.

day_by_day.notes: The walk behind Seljalandsfoss may be closed in winter due to ice — confirm with your guide on the day. Secret Lagoon is open year-round and rarely crowded on Sunday mornings in January. Bring a waterproof bag for cameras near the waterfalls.

day_by_day.morning: Full day excursion to the South Coast. Begin with a visit to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — one of the world's most dramatic beaches, with towering basalt columns, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and powerful Atlantic waves. Explore with your private guide who will brief on wave safety (sneaker waves are a serious hazard).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — a surreal landscape of floating blue icebergs calved from the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier. In January, the lagoon may be partially frozen, creating an ethereal icy silence. Nearby Diamond Beach offers the spectacle of ice chunks washed ashore on black sand, glittering like diamonds.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return journey westward as darkness falls. Stop at the Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon viewpoint (a short detour) if road conditions allow. Return to your boutique accommodation. This is a long driving day — approximately 5–6 hours total driving — so a private driver is strongly recommended.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your boutique hotel to maximize daylight hours (sunrise ~11:30, sunset ~15:30 in this region in January).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Suður-Vík Restaurant in Vík — a cozy, well-regarded spot serving traditional Icelandic fish soup, lamb stew, and fresh-baked bread. Perfect for warming up after Reynisfjara.
meals.dinner: Late dinner back near your accommodation. Try Strikið or a local countryside restaurant offering lamb rack with root vegetables and a curated Icelandic wine list.

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest excursion day of the trip — approximately 500km round trip from Southern Iceland base. A private driver or premium guided day tour is essential. Road conditions in January can be challenging (black ice, snow). Monitor road.is before departure. Jökulsárlón is approximately 4 hours from Reykjavik.

day_by_day.morning: A restful morning at your boutique accommodation after the long Day 4 drive. Enjoy a late, leisurely breakfast and a spa treatment if available at the property. Take a short walk around the local countryside in the morning light (sunrise around 11:00–11:30).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Kerið Volcanic Crater — a stunning 3,000-year-old volcanic caldera with a vivid aquamarine lake at its base, located conveniently on the Golden Circle route. In winter, the crater rim may be snow-dusted, creating a dramatic contrast. Then visit the Laugarvatn Fontana Geothermal Baths — a small, premium geothermal spa on the shores of Lake Laugarvatn with indoor steam rooms and outdoor pools fed by natural hot springs.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt Tour — your second dedicated aurora chase of the trip. January offers some of the best aurora conditions of the year with up to 18+ hours of darkness. Your expert guide will drive to optimal dark-sky locations based on the evening's forecast.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent late breakfast at the boutique hotel — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh Icelandic pastries, and a Skyr smoothie.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Laugarvatn Fontana's café — try their famous rye bread (hverabrauð) baked underground in the hot spring sand, served with Icelandic butter and smoked trout.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Matur og Drykkur in Reykjavik (if making a city trip) — a celebrated restaurant specializing in reinvented traditional Icelandic dishes, including cod's head and fermented shark for the adventurous. Alternatively, private chef dinner arranged at your boutique property.

day_by_day.notes: Laugarvatn Fontana is a more intimate and authentic alternative to Blue Lagoon — highly recommended for a second geothermal soak. Book in advance. The rye bread tasting experience is a unique cultural highlight not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer to Reykjavik for a city exploration day. Check into a premium Reykjavik city hotel for 1–2 nights (e.g., 101 Hotel or CenterHotel Þingholt) or keep your Southern base and day-trip. Begin with a visit to Hallgrímskirkja Church — Iceland's iconic Lutheran cathedral with panoramic city views from the tower. Walk Skólavörðustígur street lined with galleries and artisan shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join the Icelandic Food Tasting Walking Tour — a premium guided experience through Reykjavik's vibrant food scene. Sample traditional Icelandic delicacies including skyr, pylsur (Icelandic hot dogs), hákarl (fermented shark), kleinur doughnuts, and local craft beers. Visit the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends) or Grandi harbor district's food hall.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavik's world-class dining scene for dinner. Afterward, visit the Harpa Concert Hall for an evening performance if available — this stunning glass-facade concert hall on the harbor is an architectural marvel and hosts regular concerts and cultural events in January.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel before the transfer, or at Brauð & Co bakery in Reykjavik — famous for their cinnamon buns and sourdough.
meals.lunch: Included tastings on the Icelandic Food Tasting Walking Tour. Supplement with a bowl of lobster soup at Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) — a Reykjavik institution.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dill Restaurant — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a Nordic New Wave tasting menu celebrating Icelandic ingredients and foraging traditions. Advance reservation essential.

day_by_day.notes: Dill Restaurant requires booking weeks or months in advance — confirm reservation before travel. Harpa Concert Hall events vary — check schedule at harpa.is. The food walking tour typically runs 3 hours and covers approximately 2km on foot — wear warm, waterproof boots.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Reykjavik. Morning visit to the National Museum of Iceland — an excellent introduction to Icelandic history, sagas, and culture, particularly rewarding in winter when outdoor activities are limited by weather. Then explore the colorful streets of the old town (Tjörnin lake area, government buildings, and street art).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Perlan Museum — a futuristic glass dome building on Öskjuhlíð hill offering panoramic 360° views of Reykjavik and surroundings. Inside, explore the Wonders of Iceland exhibition including a real indoor ice cave, northern lights planetarium show, and interactive glacier exhibit. A world-class museum experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Southern Iceland boutique accommodation (or stay a second night in Reykjavik). If returning south, keep eyes on the aurora forecast — the drive back through dark countryside offers spontaneous aurora viewing opportunities. Final Northern Lights Hunt Tour if aurora forecast is strong (KP ≥ 3).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Reykjavik hotel or at Sandholt Bakery — one of Reykjavik's finest artisan bakeries, offering French-Icelandic pastries and excellent coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) — a premium restaurant near the old harbor serving dry-aged Icelandic beef, reindeer, and lamb over an open lava-rock grill. Excellent wine list.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Óx — an intimate, 12-seat counter dining experience by the Dill team, offering a hyper-seasonal tasting menu. Alternatively, Fiskfélagið (Fish Company) for exceptional Icelandic seafood fusion.

day_by_day.notes: Perlan's northern lights planetarium show is an excellent backup if real aurora viewing is hampered by cloud cover. Book Perlan tickets online in advance. If driving back to Southern Iceland in the evening, check road conditions on road.is — Route 1 (Ring Road) is generally well-maintained but can be icy.

day_by_day.morning: Back at your Southern Iceland boutique base. Morning snowshoe or winter hiking experience in the Þórsmörk nature reserve (weather and road conditions permitting — requires a super-jeep in winter). Þórsmörk sits between three glaciers and offers dramatic volcanic valley scenery. Arrange through a premium guided tour operator.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Seljavallalaug geothermal pool — one of Iceland's oldest and most secluded swimming pools, built in 1923, tucked into a mountain valley near Skógar. A 15-minute hike through a stunning gorge leads to this hidden gem. The pool is free, naturally heated, and utterly magical in the winter silence.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at your boutique accommodation. Enjoy the hotel's private hot tub or sauna under the open sky. If the aurora forecast is favorable (check en.vedur.is), tonight is a perfect opportunity for private aurora viewing from the property grounds away from any light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at your boutique hotel — hearty preparation for an active day.
meals.lunch: Packed luxury lunch from the hotel for the Þórsmörk excursion, or stop at a local café in Hvolsvöllur on the return.
meals.dinner: Private in-room or dining room dinner at your boutique accommodation — request a special chef's menu featuring local lamb, Arctic char, and seasonal Icelandic vegetables.

day_by_day.notes: Þórsmörk is only accessible in winter via super-jeep (4WD river crossings required) — book through a reputable operator such as Midgard Adventure or Iceland Mountain Guides. Seljavallalaug pool requires a short hike — trail may be icy, bring microspikes. The pool has basic changing facilities only.

day_by_day.morning: Premium glacier hiking experience on Sólheimajökull glacier — a dramatic outlet glacier of the Mýrdalsjökull ice cap, easily accessible from the South Coast. Your certified glacier guide will equip you with crampons, ice axes, and helmets for a 3–4 hour guided hike across the ice, exploring crevasses, ice caves, and moulins. One of Iceland's most iconic winter adventures.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the glacier hike, warm up with a visit to the nearby Skógafoss waterfall and the Skógar Folk Museum — one of Iceland's finest open-air museums with historic turf houses, a church, and maritime exhibits. Then drive to the Dyrhólaey Peninsula viewpoint (weather permitting) for dramatic coastal cliffs and arch views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your boutique accommodation. Treat yourself to a long soak in the hotel hot tub. Enjoy a quiet evening with dinner at the hotel. Check aurora forecast for a potential late-night viewing session.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your boutique hotel — energy-rich meal before the glacier hike (porridge, eggs, protein).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Skógar Guesthouse café near the waterfall, or a packed lunch from your hotel consumed at the glacier base.
meals.dinner: Dinner at your boutique hotel or at Eldstó Art Café in Kirkjubæjarklaustur — a charming, intimate restaurant serving home-cooked Icelandic food in a historic setting.

day_by_day.notes: Glacier hiking requires moderate fitness — no technical experience needed but participants must be able to walk on uneven terrain for 3–4 hours. Minimum age typically 10+. Book through Arctic Adventures, Icelandic Mountain Guides, or Midgard Adventure. All equipment provided. Dress in warm, waterproof layers — the glacier is significantly colder than surrounding areas.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at your boutique accommodation. Enjoy a late breakfast and a morning spa treatment or yoga session if offered by the property. Take a gentle walk in the surrounding countryside as daylight appears (around 11:00).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs area — note: the F-road (F208) to Landmannalaugar is typically closed in January due to snow and ice. Instead, arrange a premium Super Jeep tour that can access this area via alternative routes. Trek through the rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains and reach the legendary natural geothermal hot spring pool, soaking in 38°C waters surrounded by snow-covered lava fields. A truly extraordinary highland experience unique to Iceland.
day_by_day.evening: Return from the highlands as darkness falls. Warm dinner at your boutique accommodation. This is one of the most remote and magical experiences of the trip — celebrate with a special bottle of Icelandic craft spirits or a local wine pairing dinner.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full breakfast at your boutique hotel — smoked salmon eggs Benedict, fresh Icelandic pastries, and premium coffee.
meals.lunch: Packed hot lunch provided by your Super Jeep tour operator, consumed at Landmannalaugar — thermos soups, warm sandwiches, and hot chocolate in the highland wilderness.
meals.dinner: Special celebratory dinner at your boutique hotel — request the chef's signature tasting menu with wine pairing. Alternatively, dinner at Hótel Rangá's fine dining restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar in January requires a specialist Super Jeep operator — this is a remote, challenging winter expedition. Operators include Reykjavik Excursions (Super Jeep) or private operators. Confirm availability and road conditions well in advance. Bring a swimsuit and towel for the hot spring soak — changing facilities are basic (a small hut). The combination of snow, steam, and colorful mountains is utterly unforgettable.

day_by_day.morning: Morning excursion to the Westman Islands (Vestmannaeyjar) — accessible by ferry (approximately 35 minutes from Landeyjahöfn) or by a short domestic flight from Reykjavik. The islands are dramatic volcanic outcroppings formed as recently as 1963 (Surtsey Island) and 1973 (Eldfell eruption on Heimaey). Explore the Eldheimar Museum — a world-class museum built around a house excavated from the 1973 lava flow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Heimaey island — visit the Stafkirkjan Viking church, the harbor, and the famous puffin cliffs (puffins are absent in January but the cliffs remain dramatic). Hike up Eldfell volcano for panoramic views over the island and surrounding ocean. Return by ferry or flight to the mainland.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Southern Iceland boutique accommodation. Final Northern Lights Hunt Tour of the trip — your guide will make one last dedicated aurora chase into the dark countryside. January's long nights and frequent geomagnetic activity make this a prime aurora month.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your boutique hotel before the Westman Islands departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Einsi Kaldi Restaurant on Heimaey — the islands' best restaurant, serving fresh local fish and seafood caught that morning, with views over the harbor.
meals.dinner: Dinner at your boutique accommodation or a nearby countryside restaurant. Celebrate the penultimate full day with a special meal — Icelandic lamb rack with root vegetable purée and a bottle of fine Burgundy.

day_by_day.notes: Ferry to Westman Islands: check Herjólfur ferry schedule at herjolfur.is — crossings can be cancelled in rough winter weather. A domestic flight via Eagle Air from Reykjavik domestic airport is a more reliable winter alternative. Book well in advance. The Eldheimar Museum is one of Iceland's finest — allow at least 90 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day. Morning visit to a local geothermal greenhouse in the Hveragerði area — Iceland's 'hot spring town' where geothermal energy heats greenhouses producing tomatoes, cucumbers, and flowers year-round. Take a guided geothermal walk through Hveragerði's steaming hot spring valley (Reykjadalur — the hot spring river valley, though the hike to the bathing river is approximately 3km each way and may be icy in January).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Blue Lagoon for a final premium soak — this time book the exclusive Retreat Spa at Blue Lagoon, the ultimate luxury experience with private lagoon access, in-water treatments, and a Michelin-recommended restaurant. A perfect final afternoon indulgence.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer back to Reykjavik or remain at your Southern Iceland boutique property for a final night. Farewell dinner at one of Iceland's finest establishments. Pack and prepare for tomorrow's departure.

meals.breakfast: Final full Icelandic breakfast at your boutique hotel — savor every bite of the skyr, smoked fish, and fresh pastries.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa — enjoy the in-water sparkling wine and small bites service, or dine at the Retreat Restaurant overlooking the private lagoon.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Óx or Dill Restaurant in Reykjavik (if not already visited), or at Hótel Rangá for a final celebration of Icelandic cuisine. Order the full tasting menu with wine pairing — a fitting conclusion to a luxury Icelandic journey.

day_by_day.notes: The Retreat at Blue Lagoon is the most exclusive tier of the Blue Lagoon experience — access is limited and must be booked months in advance. Cost is significantly higher than standard Blue Lagoon entry but includes exclusive lagoon access, spa treatments, and dining. Confirm all bookings before travel. Tonight, do a final aurora check — if skies are clear, step outside for one last look up.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Leisurely checkout from your boutique accommodation. If time allows before your flight, take a short drive to a nearby viewpoint for a final look at the Icelandic landscape — the snow-covered mountains, steaming geothermal vents, and vast volcanic plains that make this country unlike anywhere else on Earth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Browse the Duty Free for Icelandic souvenirs — Brennivín aquavit, Icelandic sea salt, Omnom chocolate, and hand-knitted lopapeysa wool sweaters.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days — aurora dances, geothermal soaks, glacier hikes, volcanic landscapes, and world-class Nordic cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at your boutique hotel or a packed breakfast for the road.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Keflavík Airport — the airport has improved dining options including Icelandic fish and chips, lamb soup, and the Duty Free café.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for the transfer to Keflavík — from Southern Iceland, the drive is approximately 1–1.5 hours in good conditions, but winter weather can extend this. A private transfer is strongly recommended over public bus for a luxury trip. Confirm your transfer booking the evening before. Iceland's VAT refund (for purchases over 6,000 ISK) can be claimed at the airport — keep receipts.
